title: Global and local scopes are fully independent streams with their own operation logs and indices
content:
The global/local split is not a partition of one log — it is two logs. Each scope has its own state shape, its own operation sequence, and its own indices:

```ts
doc.state.global;      // shared with everyone
doc.state.local;       // yours alone

doc.operations.global; // replicated log
doc.operations.local;  // local-only log
```

The operation at index 5 in `global` has **nothing to do** with index 5 in `local`. The two counters advance independently, so you cannot interleave them, compare them, or use one as a proxy for document age. There is no global ordering across the pair, and none is needed: the Reactor's sync engine replicates `global` across peers and leaves `local` completely alone.

The practical consequences:

- **Indexing is per scope.** When asserting on an operation in a test, the index counts dispatches *into that scope*, not total dispatches against the document. A document with 3 local operations and 1 global operation has the global one at `operations.global[0]`.
- **A local dispatch is a dead end by design.** Updating your "show completed" filter appends to the local log, runs the local reducer, and stops. Teammates never see it — no sync traffic, no operation for peers to replay.
- **Revisions track separately.** Per-scope revision tracking follows from per-scope logs; there is no single document revision number spanning both.

This is also why moving a field between scopes is a schema change rather than a config toggle: you are moving it between two different histories.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/03-document-models/02-state-and-scopes.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
